title: Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (BC28): Run AL objects and open record references using fully qualified names (Support for namespaces and fully qualified names)
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (BC28) adds support for namespaces and fully qualified names in AL, allowing developers to run codeunits, pages, and reports and open table references using fully qualified names instead of numeric IDs. This feature helps organize code into logical groups and prevents naming conflicts when libraries are combined.
key_points: New method overloads enable running codeunits, pages, and reports using fully qualified names like 'Microsoft.Sales.Posting."Sales-Post"'
RecordRef.Open can now be invoked with the fully qualified name of a table
Record and RecordRef instances expose a new FullyQualifiedName property
Namespaces organize code into logical groups and hierarchies to prevent naming conflicts and enable name reuse across different contexts
features: Fully qualified names for AL objects
Running codeunits by fully qualified name
Running pages by fully qualified name
Running reports by fully qualified name
Opening table references by fully qualified name

quotes.text: Namespaces are used to organize code into logical groups and hierarchies, which can prevent naming conflicts that can occur when libraries are combined.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core benefit of namespaces for managing code complexity and library integration in Business Central development
